description: Passionate engineering innovators bridging hardware, code, and NASA open data to build real-world solutions for Earth and beyond.
summary:
As an undergraduate electronics engineering student, I have always been fascinated by how space technology can solve everyday problems right here on the ground. That drive led me to build SmartAgri Node—a custom 4-layer ESP32-C3 environmental sensing PCB designed from scratch in KiCad, paired with a live Ground-to-Orbit web dashboard.

While NASA datasets like POWER (~50 km) and SMAP (9 km) provide vital regional weather and soil baselines, their coarse resolution cannot capture microclimate shifts inside an individual farm. To close that gap, I engineered an off-grid hardware node featuring onboard climate (BME280), sunlight (TEMT6000), and acoustic pest-monitoring (MAX4466) sensors, soil-probe expansion headers, solar/LiPo power-path management (MCP73871), and microSD logging for rural connectivity dead zones. My web dashboard fuses this real-time field telemetry with NASA POWER historical data to ground-truth satellite estimates and trigger practical irrigation advisories.

Smallholder farmers face growing climate uncertainty without access to expensive precision tools. By making SmartAgri Node completely open-source, I want to put reliable, satellite-calibrated farm intelligence directly into the hands of the communities that need it most.
details:
Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data
An open-hardware field node that ground-truths NASA Earth observations at the scale of a single field.

Short summary
SmartAgri Node is an open-source, 4-layer ESP32-C3 board that measures temperature, humidity, pressure, light and sound at the crop, logs everything offline, and runs unattended on solar power. It bridges the gap between NASA's regional grids (POWER at about 50 km, SMAP soil moisture at 9 km) and what a farmer actually experiences in a field, so satellite data can be validated and acted on locally.

Full description

The problem. NASA Earth data is transforming agriculture, but its grids are coarse. A single 9 km SMAP cell can contain irrigated and rain-fed plots, shaded orchards and dry slopes, and a smallholder farmer can't act on one averaged number. Field-level microclimates and soil shifts disappear in the average.

Our solution. SmartAgri Node puts a low-cost ground-truth sensor at the plant, with a measurement footprint under 10 m. It is built around the ESP32-C3-WROOM-02-H4, a RISC-V MCU with Wi-Fi and BLE and no external radio module. Onboard sensing covers:

  • climate (BME280)
  • ambient light (TEMT6000)
  • sound (MAX4466 mic amplifier)

I2C and GPIO headers accept soil moisture, pH and EC probes. A 32 Mbit SPI flash and a microSD slot keep every reading safe in connectivity dead zones, and the node syncs over Wi-Fi when a connection is available.

Engineered for the field. An MCP73871 power-path charges a LiPo from USB-C or a solar panel while the node keeps running, so it can be installed and left alone. USB ESD protection, a resettable fuse and a regulated 3.3 V rail protect it outdoors. A 4-layer Signal/GND/PWR/Signal stackup, designed in KiCad, keeps RF and power noise away from the analog sensors.

How it uses NASA data. The node is designed to pair its readings with NASA POWER weather and solar data and NASA SMAP soil moisture for the same place and time. That lets farmers and researchers check satellite estimates against measurements and turn them into local decisions, such as irrigating before soil moisture falls below 40%. The microphone input is designed to flag unusual insect activity early, and the SPI flash supports over-the-air updates so a fleet can be improved remotely.

Why it matters. Everything is MIT-licensed, with the KiCad files and BOM public, so schools, co-ops and farms can build and extend it. It is aimed at climate-resilient smallholder farms.

Tools and technologies: KiCad, ESP32-C3, BME280, TEMT6000, MAX4466, MCP73871, CP2102N, microSD and SPI flash. NASA data: SMAP soil moisture and POWER.
